_note: The state-backed presentation machine — normalization + dismissal topology, pinned across the three runtimes (see README.md). steps = present/dismiss verb sequences; modal = the expected nav.modal ledger afterwards (order = presentation order). Normalization: `as` ∈ {sheet, cover, overlay}, anything else fails open to sheet; `touch` rides ONLY overlay entries — 'block' is pinned, anything else (or absent) fails open to 'passthrough'; chain entries (sheet/cover) never carry touch. Topology: dismiss() pops the top of the presentation stack; dismissing an OVERLAY takes only itself; dismissing a CHAIN entry takes its later chain descendants and spares every overlay; a target matches by component tag or by `as` mode, deepest-last wins; dismiss on empty is a no-op. PLANES (host contract, documented in screen-presentation.md): content stack < overlay plane (presentation order) < chain plane — a drawer/sheet always renders ABOVE a menu-bar overlay regardless of presentation order. THE ATTRIBUTE CONTRACT: `attrs` on present/push are the component's INPUT — the same attributes a hard-coded tag invocation would carry, seeded into the reactive dsx.attribute dict — and they ride the ledger entry VERBATIM (restore truth). The `update` verb ({ update: { target?, attrs } }) merges attrs into the deepest-last entry matching by component tag or `as` mode (no target = the top of the presentation stack; unmatched target = documented no-op) — entries are REPLACED, never mutated in place, and the live surface re-seeds so bindings recalc and `<attribute on:change>` fires. `vars` is the legacy store-seed channel, untouched by update.
